title: Matrices
prerequisites: Comfort with arrays of numbers in rows and columns.
Ability to solve simultaneous linear equations.
Understanding of ordered pairs and indices.

topics.title: Matrices and Their Operations
topics.quick_summary: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers; addition requires equal orders, and multiplication requires the columns of the first to match the rows of the second.
topics.real_life: Every image on a screen is a matrix of pixel values, and rotating or brightening it is a matrix operation.

detailed.definition: A matrix of order m × n has m rows and n columns. Element aᵢⱼ lies in the ith row and jth column. Two matrices are equal if they have the same order and all corresponding elements are equal.
detailed.key_idea: Matrix multiplication is not commutative: AB is generally not equal to BA, and one may be defined while the other is not. This is the single biggest departure from ordinary algebra.
detailed.working_principle: For AB to be defined, the number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B, and the product has order (rows of A) × (columns of B).
applications: Solving simultaneous equations by writing them as AX = B.
Computer graphics uses matrices for rotation, scaling and translation.
Transition matrices model how a system moves between states over time.

points: Order m × n means m rows and n columns — rows first, always.
Addition and subtraction require matrices of exactly the same order.
AB is defined only if columns of A = rows of B.
AB ≠ BA in general; matrix multiplication is not commutative.
Types: row, column, square, diagonal, scalar, identity, zero.
mistakes: Multiplying matrices element by element instead of row by column.
Writing the order as columns × rows.
topics.memory_hook: 'Rows first, columns second' — and 'inner dimensions must match, outer dimensions give the answer'.
topics.advanced: Matrix multiplication is non-commutative because it represents the composition of transformations, and rotating then reflecting is genuinely different from reflecting then rotating. The algebra is encoding geometry.

formulas.name: Matrix Multiplication
formulas.variables: aᵢₖ = element of A in row i, column k; bₖⱼ = element of B in row k, column j.
formulas.when_to_use: Whenever two compatible matrices are multiplied.
formulas.common_mistakes: Multiplying corresponding elements instead of taking row-by-column sums.
formulas.shortcut: (m×n)(n×p) gives an (m×p) matrix; the inner n must match.

topics.title: Determinants and the Inverse of a Matrix
topics.quick_summary: The determinant of a square matrix is a single number that decides whether the matrix has an inverse, and the inverse exists exactly when the determinant is non-zero.
topics.real_life: A system of equations has a unique solution exactly when its coefficient determinant is non-zero — engineers check this before attempting to solve.

detailed.definition: For a 2×2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]], the determinant is ad − bc. A matrix is singular if its determinant is zero and non-singular otherwise. The inverse A⁻¹ satisfies AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I.
detailed.key_idea: The determinant is the gatekeeper. If it is zero the matrix has no inverse, and the corresponding system of equations has either no solution or infinitely many.
detailed.working_principle: For a 2×2 matrix, the inverse is (1/det A) × adj A, where the adjoint is obtained by swapping the diagonal elements and changing the signs of the off-diagonal ones.
applications: AX = B has the unique solution X = A⁻¹B when det A ≠ 0.
The determinant of a 2×2 matrix is the area of the parallelogram formed by its rows.

points: A⁻¹ exists if and only if det A ≠ 0.
For a 2×2 matrix, A⁻¹ = (1/det A)[[d, −b], [−c, a]].
AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I, the identity matrix.
mistakes: Swapping the wrong pair of elements when forming the adjoint of a 2×2 matrix.
Attempting to invert a singular matrix.
Writing (AB)⁻¹ = A⁻¹B⁻¹; the order must be reversed.
topics.memory_hook: 'Swap the diagonal, flip the signs off it, divide by the determinant.'
topics.advanced: Geometrically the determinant is the factor by which a transformation scales area. A zero determinant means the transformation collapses the plane onto a line, which is exactly why the information needed to invert it has been lost.

formulas.name: Inverse of a 2×2 Matrix
formulas.variables: A = [[a, b], [c, d]], with ad − bc ≠ 0.
formulas.when_to_use: To solve AX = B, or wherever a matrix inverse is required.
formulas.common_mistakes: Negating the diagonal elements instead of the off-diagonal ones.
formulas.shortcut: Swap a and d, negate b and c, then divide by the determinant.
